item.title: Current Events - November 18, 2026
item.description:
November 18, 2026 (2026-11-18) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian War
    • Crimea attacks
      • 2026 Crimean Bridge explosions
        • The Crimean Bridge connecting Taman, Russia, and Kerch, Russian-occupied Crimea, is struck by Ukrainian forces for the third time in four days, prompting Russian authorities to close the bridge to all traffic. (AP) (The Guardian)
  • Haitian conflict
    • Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
      • Salvadoran forces destroy a house belonging to Jeff Larose, the leader of the Taliban gang that operates in Canaan, Haiti. The Gang Suppression Force says it was not involved. (AP)
  • Aftermath of the July Uprising
    • Two Bangladesh Nationalist Party members are killed when suspected members of the banned Awami League attack a motorcycle procession in Narail District, Bangladesh. (Daily Sun)
    • A crowd led by Chatra Dal members storms and sets fire to the residence of former Awami League Member of Parliament Shamim Osman in Narayanganj District, while unidentified attackers loot and set fire to two houses belonging to former Minister of Fisheries and Livestock SM Rezaul Karim in Pirojpur District. Separately, arsonists burn the residence of former Minister of Foreign Affairs Dipu Moni in Chandpur, and a crowd in Sirajganj vandalises the local Awami League office and the residence of former MP Habibe Millat. (Views Bangladesh) (The Daily Star) (The Daily Star)
    • In Gopalganj District, armed members of the banned Awami League, Chhatra League, and Jubo League detonate crude bombs and set fire to a private clinic owned by BNP Member of Parliament K M Babar of Gopalganj-2, forcing patients to evacuate. Attackers also burn at least five BNP offices across Muksudpur and Kashiani and target two Grameen Bank branches. (Dhaka Tribune)
  • Gaza war
    • The Israeli army launches its first operation in central Gaza Strip amid the displacement of families from the area, for the first time since the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025 came into effect. (BBC News)
  • Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
    • A militant commander is killed by the Indian Armed Forces at a mosque in Kulgam district, Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, after escaping a shootout with troops two days earlier in a neighboring village, where his associate was killed. (AP)
  • Mexican drug war
    • An operation against cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion cells in Zapopan, Jalisco left three gunmen killed and three arrested, including a ringleader. Authorities concluded the operation after seven hours of gunfight. (Nmás)

Arts and culture

  • Vincent van Gogh's 1890 painting Blossoming Chestnut Trees sells for US$190.4 million at Sotheby's in New York City, United States, setting a new auction record for Van Gogh and surpassing the $117.2 million paid for Orchard with Cypresses (1888) in 2022. (AFP via NDTV)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • In Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, Bangladesh, thousands of garment workers demanding a monthly minimum wage increase from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240) block the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway and set fire to a police vehicle, causing police to fire tear gas and stun grenades in Gazipur and Ashulia as 55 factories close across the three areas, while police report around 300 arrests across 24 cases filed in Savar and Ashulia during the protests. (The Daily Star)
    • In Kafrul, Dhaka, police fire around ten stun grenades against demonstrating garment workers following clashes with Bangladesh Nationalist Party activists who allegedly harassed female factory employees, causing workers to stage demonstrations and halt production at several nearby garment factories. (The Business Standard)

International relations

  • Operation Southern Spear
    • Colombia–United States relations
      • United States secretary of defense Pete Hegseth formally delivers a Lockheed C-130 Hercules to Colombia during a visit to the country to discuss military cooperation, including against drug cartels. (The Hill)
    • United States–Venezuela relations
      • United States secretary of defense Pete Hegseth and acting Venezuelan president Delcy Rodríguez sign a military cooperation agreement that includes joint training and intelligence sharing between the United States and Venezuelan armed forces. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Arsonists set fire to the ancestral home of former chief adviser Muhammad Yunus in Panchlaish, Chattogram, Bangladesh. (The Daily Star)

Science and technology

  • NASA's space probe Voyager 1 reaches the distance of one light-day from Earth, being the first man-made object to reach that distance, after it launched in 1977. (CNN)
  • PlayStation reports a major outage ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. (Axios)

Sports

  • Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2026–27
    • In Test cricket, Bangladeshi wicketkeeper Litton Das sets a world record for the most dismissals in a single Test innings, recording six catches and two stumpings against South Africa in Johannesburg. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - November 11, 2026
item.description:
November 11, 2026 (2026-11-11) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
        • Iran attacks ship navigation systems on Didamar Island, Oman. Unknown damage is caused. (Reuters)
    • Gaza war
      • Attacks on health facilities during the Gaza war
        • Israel launches an airstrike against the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, killing six Palestinians, including a surgeon, and wounding over 20 more. Four more people are also killed in other airstrikes in the Gaza Strip. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Allied Democratic Forces insurgency, Ituri war
    • At least 22 people are killed by Islamic State-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces rebels across eight locations in Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. (AP)
  • Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
    • Three Central Reserve Police Force personnel are injured after militants open fire on a checkpoint near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. Security forces launch a search operation to locate the attackers. (Gulf News) (The Hindu)
  • Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
    • Pakistani Taliban carries out an ambush against police personnel in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing ten officers. Eighteen gunmen are also killed in the ensuing shootout. (AP)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis, German economic crisis
    • The German cabinet approves draft legislation establishing a strategic natural gas reserve of 24 terawatt-hours, equivalent to approximately 10% of national storage capacity, to maintain gas supplies during emergencies. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
    • The Central Bank of Paraguay reports providing partial refunds to 1,812,348 eligible Ueno Bank depositors following the bank's collapse. (France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–27 European windstorm season
    • Portugal closes approximately 8,000 schools nationwide and suspends non-essential public services as Storm Charles approaches. The second day of the Web Summit in Lisbon is also cancelled. (AP) (Deadline)
  • 2026 New York City building collapse
    • A 3-story apartment building collapses near a construction site in Brooklyn, New York City, United States, killing eight people and wounding 19 more. (AFP) (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Kenyan health ministry reports that the country has discharged its last Ebola patient from a hospital in Nairobi after eleven contact cases were treated. Kenya will be declared Ebola-free on December 23 if no one else exhibits symptoms. (DW)
    • The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 11,000, with at least 5,387 deaths, affecting 8 of the country's 26 provinces. (Al Jazeera)
  • The American ocean liner SS United States is sunk off the coast of Destin–Fort Walton Beach, Florida, United States, to become the world's largest artificial reef. (Pensacola News Journal) (Reuters)

International relations

  • Argentina–Iran relations
    • Iran designates the Argentinian naval and air forces as terrorist organizations, in response to Argentina designating the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as such in March. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • China–Germany relations
    • Germany announces that its military will discontinue using Chinese-made drones for military training and exercises, replacing them with German or other European models to address security concerns. (AP) (Reuters)
  • France–Russia relations
    • Russia bans two French lawmakers, Arthur Delaporte and Sacha Houlié, and two journalists, Ariane Chemin and Paul Gogo, from entering the country for allegedly harassing Xenia Fedorova, the head of RT France, from 2017 to 2023. (Al Jazeera)
  • Kenya–Sudan relations
    • Kenyan president William Ruto signs a deal for Sudan to lift its 20-month ban on imports of tea from Kenya. (Business Daily Africa)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European infrastructure disruption
    • European bomb threat wave
      • More than 6,000 schools across Italy are evacuated following bomb threats. (BBC News) (Reuters)
  • Colombian conflict
    • Two people are arrested in connection with an explosive attack on the headquarters of Colombian broadcaster RCN Televisión in Cali, Valle del Cauca. (AFP via Gulf News)
  • Former Red Brigades member Leonardo Bertulazzi escapes house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina, while awaiting extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence for kidnapping and membership in an armed group. Argentine security forces launch a manhunt for him. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 United States Senate elections
    • 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi
      • After a week of counting affidavit ballots, the Associated Press and CNN project the election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi for Democratic candidate Scott Colom, defeating the incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith and becoming the first black senator from the state since Blanche Bruce in the 1874–75 elections. (AFP) (AP) (CNN)
  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • The Brazilian Superior Electoral Court fines Meta Platforms R$7.5 million (US$1.34 million) for failing to comply with judicial orders concerning the 2026 presidential election, while finding insufficient evidence of deliberate electoral interference. (AFP via Le Monde)
  • 2026 Spanish housing protests
    • Millions of workers across Spain launch a general strike to demand government intervention over the country's housing crisis, as an escalation of the ongoing protests. (Al Jazeera) (El País)
  • Gibran Rakabuming Raka diploma controversy
    • Indonesian vice president Gibran Rakabuming Raka submits his resignation amid questions about his educational qualifications. Bloomberg News reports that President Prabowo Subianto accepts the resignation, although the government has not publicly confirmed its acceptance. (Reuters)
  • Independence March
    • Polish president Karol Nawrocki and at least 500,000 people participate in the annual patriotic march celebrating the National Independence Day in Warsaw, Poland. (Zero in Polish)

Science and technology

  • Cyberwarfare by Russia
    • The Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) reports that it stopped a December 2025 cyberattack against an unidentified government institution, attributing it to the Russia-linked trojan package Turla. The SRI finds no evidence that sensitive information was stolen. (Reuters)
  • Cybersecurity firm CloudSek reports that the Kazakhstan-linked hacker group Silent Lynx used an autonomous agent to breach Tajikistan's government database and steal more than 2,000 national security-related documents. (The Record) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup
    • The United States men's national under-17 soccer team withdraws from the upcoming FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar, citing safety concerns related to the Houthi–Saudi conflict. (AFP) (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - November 24, 2026
item.description:
November 24, 2026 (2026-11-24) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Zaporizhzhia strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Russian airstrike hits a five-story apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, killing two people and wounding 44 others. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Thirteen people are killed and fourteen others are injured when a bus collides with a stationary truck in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates. (Gulf News)
  • At least seven people are killed and nine others are injured in a cooking gas explosion in a residential area of Hanoi, Vietnam. (VnExpress)

Health and environment

  • Climate change in the United Kingdom
    • 2026 United Kingdom heatwaves
      • The UK Health Security Agency says it recorded the highest number of heat-related deaths in the United Kingdom on record in 2026 at 5,258, surpassing the previous record in 2022. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2025 Africa Cup of Nations
    • In association football, the Court of Arbitration for Sport rules in favor of Senegal against Morocco and reverses the Confederation of African Football's controversial decision to overturn Senegal's 1–0 victory in the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final. (AP) (The Guardian)

item.title: Current Events - November 17, 2026
item.description:
November 17, 2026 (2026-11-17) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
        • Five Palestinians are killed, including a child, and others are injured in a series of Israeli airstrikes on various areas of the Gaza Strip, Palestine. (AA)
      • Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war, Israeli settler violence
        • A 72-year-old Palestinian woman is killed and ten others are injured in an attack by Israeli settlers on Palestinian homes in the village of Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank. (Al Jazeera)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
          • Bahrain's military intercepts a number of drones fired by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) at Sheikh Isa Air Base. (Al Jazeera)
      • The United States Air Force conducts a series of at least six strikes on Qeshm Island. The IRGC says it shot down a General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper drone south of the island. (Reuters) (AFP via Le Monde)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Crimea attacks
      • The Crimean Bridge is struck by Ukrainian drones for the second day in a row, killing two people and prompting Russian authorities to close vehicle traffic again. Open-source intelligence report that a section of the road bridge damaged yesterday has collapsed into the Kerch Strait. (Reuters) (Türkiye Today)
  • Aftermath of the July Uprising
    • Following the arrest of party leaders, banned Awami League and Chhatra League activists mobilize via mosque loudspeakers to storm and burn a police station in Tungipara, Gopalganj District, Bangladesh. Amid police tear gas and rubber bullet fire, the attackers free detainees, loot firearms, burn Bangladesh Nationalist Party MP S M Jilani's (Gopalganj-3) residence, and blockade local roads. (The Daily Star) (The Business Standard)
    • In Comilla, Bangladesh, Swechhasebak Dal members burn the local Awami League office and former MP AKM Bahauddin Bahar's residence in retaliation for the attack on BNP leader S M Jilani's home. (The Business Standard)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • Bangladeshi police and 42 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh deploy tear gas, stun grenades, batons, and surveillance drones against garment workers across Dhaka, Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, and Narayanganj protesting for a minimum wage hike from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240). Protesters block the N3, N4, and N5 highways and shutter 37 factories after a Minimum Wage Board meeting is delayed to November 23. (AFP) (The Hindu)
  • Canada–China relations
    • Canada and China agree to further tariff reductions following talks between Canadian prime minister Mark Carney and Chinese leader Xi Jinping before the APEC summit in Shenzhen. China reduces tariffs on C$400 million (¥1.8 billion) in Canadian exports, while Canada extends relief for Chinese steel and aluminium. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crash
    • A Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crashes near Kemerovo, Russia, killing all 19 people on board. (AP) (The Independent)
  • Forty-six people are injured after a collision between two trains in Prague, Czech Republic. (BBC News)
  • A small boat reportedly carrying about a hundred people, mostly migrants, capsizes off Yenne, Senegal. Various sources report that either at least four or lesser bodies have been recovered, as several others are still missing. Search operations are launched by authorities. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • Measles resurgence in the Americas
    • The Pan American Health Organization revokes the measles elimination statuses of Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States. For the U.S., the organization cited continuous domestic transmission for over 12 months amid more than 5,700 reported infections and multiple deaths in 2026. (AFP via France 24) (Al Jazeera)

International relations

  • France–Malaysia relations
    • France and Malaysia establish a strategic partnership, signing agreements on defence, energy, and technology cooperation during French president Emmanuel Macron's state visit. Malaysia also agrees to permit limited exports of unprocessed rare-earth minerals to France in exchange for assistance with mineral processing. (Reuters)
  • Israel–United Kingdom relations, United Kingdom and the Gaza war
    • British foreign secretary Ed Miliband announces that the United Kingdom will sanction eight companies involved in the construction of settlements in the occupied West Bank, as well as Tzav 9 for its role in blocking humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip. (AP)

Law and crime

  • Crime in Costa Rica
    • Investigative journalist Camilo Rodríguez is shot dead in his vehicle in Santo Domingo, Heredia, Costa Rica, in the first journalist death in the country in at least 25 years. (AFP)
  • A factory worker is hacked to death after filming clashes between two factions of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party in Fatullah, Narayanganj District. (Views Bangladesh)
  • A court in Conakry, Guinea, tries over 1,000 alleged artisanal gold miners for illegal gold mining in the Siguiri region, resulting in the sentencing of 22 former regional administrators and 202 others to various prison terms. (DW)
  • The North Macedonian Agency for National Security arrests five Macedonian nationals allegedly linked to an assassination plot in Greece, allegedly involving Iranian recruiters, including Naji Sharifi-Zindashti, who is wanted by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation. A sixth person remains at large. Greek public television reports that the target was a Israeli business executive based in Athens. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • Corruption in Mongolia
    • Mongolian president Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh announces his resignation from office, three days after former Ulaanbaatar mayor Khishgeegiin Nyambaatar accused him of past embezzlement from a railway project during his tenure as prime minister. The State Great Khural must accept the resignation for it to become effective. (AP)
  • Haitian crisis, Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
    • Hundreds of Haitians march in cities across Haiti to show support for the deployment of Salvadoran troops to combat gang violence. (Al Jazeera)

Science and technology

  • American technology company Apple experiences an outage with several of its services, including Apple Pay, iCloud, the App Store, and AppleCare. The company's spokesperson attributed the problems to an internal update and rules out a cyberattack. (Time)

Sports

  • 2026 Melbourne Cup
    • Racing NSW launches an investigation after the body of losing horse So You Are is found in a skip bin in Sydney, Australia. (CNN) (The Guardian Australia)

item.title: Current Events - November 19, 2026
item.description:
November 19, 2026 (2026-11-19) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Iran's navy says that an oil tanker caught on fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz. (Al Jazeera)
      • 2026 Lebanon war
        • The Israeli Air Force strikes a Hezbollah underground facility in Lebanon's Bekaa valley. (The Times of Israel)
        • Two Israeli drones explode in Nabatieh, Lebanon, without causing any injuries. (Al Jazeera)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • The Houthis fire missiles at King Abdullah Financial District in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which damage the Public Investment Fund Tower and other buildings but cause no injuries. (Middle East Monitor) (Al-Monitor)
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • The Yemeni government's military says it has killed or injured 144 Houthi fighters during recent operations in the Taiz, Marib, and Al-Jawf governorates, and to have repelled an attack in the Tur Al Bahah area. (Al Jazeera)
        • The Houthis say that Saudi-led coalition airstrikes have killed 10 people in Sanaa, Yemen, over the past two days. (Al Jazeera)
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza's health ministry reports that two people have been killed by recent Israeli attacks and two others died from their wounds over the past day. (Al Jazeera)
  • Haitian conflict
    • The Haitian National Police say that 34 alleged gang members were killed during an operation in Port-au-Prince, in an area under the influence of the Viv Ansanm alliance, with the assistance of the Haitian government task force involving Erik Prince's private security contractors. (Reuters)
  • Aftermath of the July Uprising
    • In Bangladesh, banned Awami League members loot and burn properties in Gopalganj District, including BNP MP Md. Selimuzzaman Mollah's ancestral home, a police station, and a Grameen Bank branch, and vandalise BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami properties. Separately, attackers burn the homes of former politicians Rahim Ullah in Feni District, Shahriar Alam in Rajshahi District and Mahmud Hasan Sumon in Mymensingh District. (BSS) (The Financial Express)
    • Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 97 platoons across seven districts, with five more on standby, amid ongoing political violence and labour unrest. (The Guardian) (The Daily Star)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • Across Bangladesh, 341 garment factories remain closed amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as police fire tear gas and stun grenades to disperse demonstrators in Ashulia and clear blockades on the N3 highway in Gazipur, while Bangladesh Nationalist Party members take up positions along highway areas in Sreepur and authorities tighten security at Kashimpur Central Jail. (New Age) (The Business Standard) (Prothom Alo)
  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • The Joint Organisations Data Initiative reports that Saudi Arabia's oil exports rose in September to their highest level since the outbreak of the war in February, despite Houthi attacks on Red Sea ports and infrastructure. (Al Jazeera)
  • Economy of Senegal
    • Senegalese president Bassirou Diomaye Faye enacts the revised 2026 budget by decree after parliament rejected it, seeking to advance a proposed US$2.2 billion International Monetary Fund loan programme aimed at addressing the country's debt. (AFP via France 24)
  • Grand Theft Auto VI by Rockstar Games becomes the biggest video game launch in history with more than $2.3 billion in sales, surpassing the previous record holder, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, by more than $600 million. (LBC)

International relations

  • APEC China 2026
    • Chile–Philippines relations
      • The Philippines and Chile sign a free trade agreement as part of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, marking the former's first such agreement with a Latin American country. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)
    • China–Russia relations, China–United States relations, Russia–United States relations
      • Chinese leader Xi Jinping, Russian president Vladimir Putin, and United States president Donald Trump hold their first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen during the APEC summit and issue a joint declaration addressing nuclear war, petroleum production, and United Nations reform. (AFP) (BBC News)
  • Operation Southern Spear
    • Honduras–United States relations
      • Honduran president Nasry Asfura and United States secretary of defense Pete Hegseth sign two security cooperation agreements at Soto Cano Air Base, Honduras. (The Latin News)
  • Pakistan–Qatar relations
    • Pakistan and Qatar sign a memorandum of understanding on cooperation between their Federal Constabulary and Internal Security Force, respectively. (Al Jazeera)
  • Somalia–United Arab Emirates relations
    • Somalia expels the ambassador from the United Arab Emirates, saying the country undermined Somalia's sovereignty. (AP)

Law and crime

  • Palestinians in Israeli custody, Gaza Strip healthcare collapse
    • An Israeli court extends the detention of Gaza Strip's Kamal Edwan hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya by six months. (Al Jazeera)
  • Rohingya genocide case
    • The International Court of Justice rules that Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya people. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • 2027 Salvadoran presidential election
    • Incumbent Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele presents his presidential candidacy to the Supreme Electoral Court seeking registration ahead of the 2027 elections. He is running for a third presidential term after Bukele's government aproved constitutional amendments to abolish term limits in 2025. (AP)
  • Corruption in Mongolia
    • The State Great Khural accepts the resignation of Mongolian president Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh. The chamber's chairman, Sandagiin Byambatsogt, assumes the acting presidency until a new election is held within four months. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - November 12, 2026
item.description:
November 12, 2026 (2026-11-12) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Haitian conflict
    • Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
      • Haitian and Salvadoran soldiers take control of the Stade Sylvio Cator in Port-au-Prince after two years of gang control. (France 24)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and United States special envoy Jared Kushner announce that European representatives will join future peace negotiations with Russia, which Russian president Vladimir Putin agrees to while maintaining his territorial demands and rejecting foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine. (AFP via New Straits Times) (Reuters)
  • At least 10 people, including five with gunshot wounds, are injured in Munshiganj Sadar, Bangladesh, during a clash involving gunfire and crude bomb explosions between two factions of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party. (The Business Standard)

Arts and culture

  • Guatemala receives the remains of 1967 Nobel Prize in Literature recipient Miguel Ángel Asturias from France, 52 years after his death. President Bernardo Arévalo attends a ceremony ahead of the writer's burial in Guatemala City. (AFP)

Business and economy

  • Jensen Huang spying scandal
    • Jensen Huang resigns as chief executive officer (CEO) and president of Nvidia and leaves the company's board following reports of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese intelligence agent. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO. (AFP) (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • Fourteen people are killed and 30 more injured in a multiple-vehicle collision involving 18 cars and five trucks in the Emirate of Fujairah, United Arab Emirates. (AFP via The Daily Star) (Al Jazeera)
  • A passenger van plunges off a road in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, killing eleven people and wounding three more. (AP)
  • A bus veers off a mountain road in Bhimphedi, Nepal, killing ten people and wounding five more. (AP)
  • A military helicopter crashes in Malatya, Turkey, killing four soldiers. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • Four more children in Bangladesh are reported to have died from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,299. (BSS)

Law and crime

  • Iranian external operations
    • A British court convicts two Iranian men of spying on journalists from London-based broadcaster Iran International. One of them is also convicted of preparing a violent attack, while a third defendant is acquitted. (AFP via RFI) (AP)
  • 2026 Logan Circle shooting
    • One person is killed and four more are injured in a shooting spree in Logan Circle, Washington D.C., United States. The suspected gunman later kills himself after barricading himself from police inside a nearby apartment. (Al Jazeera) (AP)
  • Europol announces that Operation TorNado, an international investigation into illegal dark web marketplaces, resulted in 354 arrests across 14 countries and the seizure of approximately 5.7 tonnes of drugs, 209 firearms, and €211 million (US$234 million) in assets. (AFP)

Science and technology

  • A major outage impacts multiple Microsoft services, including Microsoft 365, Copilot and Teams, worldwide. (BBC News)

Sports

  • International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Finland–Russia relations, Norway–Russia relations
    • Finland announces visa restrictions preventing Russian athletes, including neutral competitors, from entering for sporting events beginning November 16. Norway also announces similar restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes and their support staff. (AFP via RFI)

item.title: Current Events - November 22, 2026
item.description:
November 22, 2026 (2026-11-22) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukrainian attacks on the Russian shadow fleet
      • Several people are killed and at least 10 others are injured after the Russian corvette Merkury is struck by a Ukrainian naval drone attack while docked at the Port of Benghazi, Libya. The Merkury later capsizes and sinks. (Al-Jazeera) (Reuters)
      • The M/V Angara, a Russian-flagged cargo ship, is also struck by naval drones off the coast of Benghazi in the Mediterranean Sea. (NPR)
  • Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
    • The Catholic World Report notes that at least 140 people were killed by Allied Democratic Forces and Islamic State Central Africa Province attacks targeting Christians in the Democratic Republic of the Congo provinces of North Kivu and Ituri over the course of two weeks earlier in November. (Catholic World Report)
  • South Sudanese Civil War
    • Twenty-four people, including seven children, are killed in an attack by the armed wing of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-in-Opposition in Tonj East County, Warrap State, South Sudan. Four attackers are also killed. (CTV News)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Four people are killed, nine others are wounded, and a United Nations building is damaged in drone attacks in Omdurman, Sudan. (AFP via Genocide Watch)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • Two people are killed and thirteen others are abducted in two separate bandit attacks in Magaji and Maru, Zamfara State, Nigeria. (TVC News)
  • Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
    • Five children are killed and another is injured in a landmine explosion in Khan Shaykhun, Idlib Governorate, Syria. (Asharq Al-Awsat)

Arts and culture

  • 63rd Golden Horse Awards
    • The 63rd Golden Horse Awards take place in Taipei, Taiwan, with the Hong Kong film We Are Born Good winning Best Narrative Feature. (AFP)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • Several garment factories in Gazipur, Bangladesh declare holidays amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as clashes erupt between workers and police along the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway, with workers throwing bricks and police firing tear gas and stun grenades while Special Response Battalion, Ansar, BGB, and Industrial Police personnel deploy to the area. (The Business Standard)
    • Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, stepping up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones using drones and police body cameras. (The Daily Star)

Disasters and accidents

  • At least twelve people are killed and 23 others are injured in two separate road accidents in Kota district, Rajasthan, India. (Xinhua)
  • A severe thunderstorm kills five people and injures more than 250 others in Tupanciretã, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. (AFP)
  • Three people are killed in a house fire in Trzcianka, Poland. (Xinhua)
  • Carbon monoxide poisoning from a suspected heater malfunction during Sunday mass at a church in Bad Grönenbach, Bavaria, Germany, leaves 56 people injured. (Der Spiegel)

Health and environment

  • 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference
    • The 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, concludes without a final agreement after countries failed to reach consensus on fossil fuel policies. It is the longest climate summit on record. (AFP) (Reuters)

International relations

  • Democratic Republic of the Congo–Kenya relations
    • Democratic Republic of the Congo president Félix Tshisekedi and Kenyan president William Ruto agree to restore full diplomatic relations after a summit in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, hosted by the country's president Denis Sassou Nguesso and mediated by Togolese former president Faure Gnassingbé. (BBC News)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Co-op Live incident
    • Around 12,000 concertgoers are evacuated from the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, England, after an unknown substance, initially believed to be tear gas, is dispersed during a Don Toliver concert, causing respiratory distress to multiple attendees. (BBC News) (CNN)

Politics and elections

  • South Korean education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigns following criticism of the government's response to artificial intelligence-assisted cheating concerns surrounding the College Scholastic Ability Test. President Lee Jae Myung accepts Choi's resignation. (AFP)

Sports

  • 2026 ATP Finals
    • In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev 6–2, 7–6(9–7) in the final to win his first singles title at the 2026 ATP Finals. (Reuters)
  • 2026 MotoGP World Championship
    • In motorcycle racing, Spanish rider Marc Márquez of Ducati Corse secures his eighth MotoGP World Championship after finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix, equalling Giacomo Agostini's record for the most premier-class motorcycle racing world titles. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - November 15, 2026
item.description:
November 15, 2026 (2026-11-15) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war
        • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that a supertanker carrying two million barrels of oil has sunk in the Strait of Hormuz after striking a mine. (AFP via Arab News)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli military says that Al-Qassam Brigades commander Samir Abu Younis of the Rafah brigade, who helped plan and oversaw the October 7 attacks on Israel, was killed in a airstrike in the southern area of Gaza Strip, with Hamas confirming his death and plans for a funeral. (Middle East Eye)
      • Three Palestinians are killed and others are injured in shelling and shooting attacks by Israeli troops in various areas of the Gaza Strip, in a continuation of the violation of the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025. (AA)
  • Communal conflicts in Nigeria
    • Religious violence in Nigeria
      • The Nigerian Defence Headquarters announces that the Nigerian Army killed eight terrorists, arrested 22 additional terrorists, logistical personnel and their families, and rescued 125 kidnapping victims in various raids in the states of Adamawa, Bauchi, Yobe, and Borno between November 6 and 12. (The Vanguard)
    • Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria
      • Three people are killed and several others are abducted in a cattle raid in Rabah, Sokoto State, Nigeria. (The Punch)
  • Somali Civil War
    • The African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia transfers control of five bases in Barawe, Lower Shabelle, to the Somali Armed Forces. (Hiiraan Online)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • Amid minimum wage protests by garment workers, 13 garment factories in Gazipur are shut indefinitely under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 and over 50 remain closed in Savar and Ashulia, while 48 platoons of the Border Guard, Ansar, and Special Response Battalion deploy across industrial zones in Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj. (The Business Standard)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twelve people are killed and 16 others are injured when a bus carrying gas refinery workers overturns in Ilam province, Iran. (IRNA English)
  • Five people are injured, including three seriously, in a suspected gas explosion and fire at a Christmas market in Maredsous, Wallonia, Belgium. (Nederlandse Omroep Stichting in Dutch)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • Eight more children in Bangladesh are reported to have died from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,314. (UNB via The Daily Star)
  • Eight more people in Bangladesh are reported to have died from dengue fever, bringing this year's outbreak's death toll to 499. (BSS)

International relations

  • Australia–Philippines relations
    • Australia and the Philippines sign a defence cooperation agreement in Manila, simplifying procedures for joint military exercises and expanding maritime surveillance, information sharing, training, and disaster response. (Reuters)
  • Estonia–Russia relations, Russian sabotage operations in Europe
    • Estonia announces the closure of its three border crossings with Russia starting December 1 after eight suspects were detained over an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which Estonian intelligence attributes to Russia's GRU. (CNN)

Law and crime

  • 2026 ASEAN Summits, Protests against Donald Trump
    • Philippine police arrest at least 287 people during nationwide protests against the potential signing of a Pax Silica deal with the United States coinciding with the 49th ASEAN Summit in Metro Manila. Police also report that 15 officers sustained injuries during demonstrations. (GMA News Online) (Rappler)
  • 2026 Karak church shooting, Capital punishment in Jordan
    • The Jordanian State Security Court sentences three men to death for an October 23 shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak Governorate that killed nine people and injured 25 others. Two accomplices receive six-year prison sentences. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Cape Verdean presidential election
    • Cape Verdeans vote to elect a president, where the main two candidates are the incumbent PAICV candidate José Maria Neves and the MpD candidate Joana Rosa. (AP)
    • Neves wins re-election to a second five-year term with 63.8% of the vote, according to provisional results from the election commission. Rosa concedes defeat. (AFP via France 24) (Inforpress in Portuguese)
  • 2026 Gagauz general election
    • Gagauzians in Moldova vote to elect a governor and 35 members of the People's Assembly. MP Alexandr Stoianoglo and Fiodor Gagauz advance to the second round after no candidate received a majority of the vote. (Radio Moldova) (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • Non-profit fanfiction repository website Archive of Our Own is restored to limited functionality 17 days after being targeted in a cyberattack. (AP)

Sports

  • 2026 WTA Finals
    • 2026 WTA Finals – Doubles
      • In tennis, Kateřina Siniaková and Taylor Townsend win their second and first WTA Finals doubles titles, respectively, after defeating Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini in the final, 6–4, 6–3. (The Desert Sun)
    • 2026 WTA Finals – Singles
      • In tennis, Mirra Andreeva wins her first WTA Finals singles title after defeating Elina Svitolina in the final, 7–5, 6–3. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 European Tour
    • In golf, Rory McIlroy equals Colin Montgomerie's record for the most Harry Vardon Trophies after winning his eighth Race to Dubai title, which McIlroy claimed after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Grey Cup
    • In Canadian football, the Edmonton Elks win their 15th Canadian Football League title after beating the Montreal Alouettes 37–30 in the Grey Cup. They previously won in 2015. (Edmonton Journal)
  • 2026 Women's Rugby League World Cup, Australia–New Zealand sports rivalries
    • In women's rugby league, Australia wins its fourth consecutive World Cup title after defeating New Zealand 34–10 in the final in Brisbane. (AFP via RFI)
  • 2026–27 UEFA Nations League
    • In association football, England defeats Spain 3–2 in the group stage of UEFA Nations League A to end Spain's 43-match unbeaten streak, the longest by a national team. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - November 21, 2026
item.description:
November 21, 2026 (2026-11-21) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza genocide, Gaza humanitarian crisis
        • Three Palestinians are killed by an Israeli drone strike on a food-carrying vehicle in Gaza City, while another is killed by gunfire in Jabalia. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters) (Al Jazeera)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • Saudi forces intercept three ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, by the Houthis. (Al Jazeera)
  • War on drugs
    • Colombian conflict
      • A bombing against a FARC dissidents camp in a rural area of Mapiripán, Meta Department, kills five guerrilla fighters. (CW+ noticias)
    • Mexican drug war
      • Four soldiers and 16 gunmen are killed in a shootout amid a federal operation by the Mexican Army in Guasave, Sinaloa, leading to the arrest of a cartel leader. (Meganoticias)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • 2026 drone incursions into the Baltic states and Finland
      • The Finnish defence ministry imposes temporary airspace and maritime restrictions after a drone struck a Russian cargo vessel in international waters of the Gulf of Finland, causing a fire. (AFP)
  • Aftermath of the July Uprising
    • Clashes between Bangladesh Nationalist Party supporters and banned Awami League activists in Bera Upazila, Pabna District, injure several people following an arson attack at the abandoned home of former Deputy Speaker Shamsul Hoque Tuku and retaliatory vandalism, with police firing rubber bullets and tear gas to disperse the crowd. (UNB)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • Between five and eleven people, including an infant, are killed, five others are injured and several others are abducted in a bandit attack in Borgu, Niger State, Nigeria. (The Punch) (AFP via Citizen Digital)
    • Between 35 and 74 Fulani herdsmen are killed in a vigilante attack in two villages of Borgu in retaliation for the earlier bandit raid. (The Rio Times)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • At least 80 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia, Bangladesh, declare general holidays after workers stage sit-ins and work stoppages over minimum wage demands, while police announce that 96 people, including five labour leaders, have been arrested in connection with the 4 November clashes on the Dhaka–Aricha Highway. (The Business Standard) (The Daily Star)
    • Laid-off garment workers in Rupganj, Narayanganj District, block roads by felling trees and burning tires over unpaid wages. (The Business Standard)
    • Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 90 platoons across seven districts, with four more on standby, amid ongoing political violence and strike action. (Dhaka Tribune)
  • Japan–Saudi Arabia relations
    • The Japanese trade ministry announces that Saudi Arabia agreed to triple the volume of crude oil stored in Japan to 24 million barrels, under Japan's joint stockpiling system with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. (Japan Today)

Disasters and accidents

  • A fire at a confectionery factory in Serang Regency, Banten, Indonesia, kills at least 24 people, leaves 30 others missing, and injures five. (Reuters)
  • Four people are killed and 35 others are injured in a fire at a power station in Basra, Iraq. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Indonesia–European Union trade relations
    • Indonesia and the European Union sign trade and investment agreements that will lift 98.5% of tariffs on EU goods. (Euronews)

Law and crime

  • Three people are killed and another person is injured in a shootout at a baby shower in Parma, Ohio, United States. The dead include one of the shooters, while a second person is arrested for killing the presumed main perpetrator. (Associated Press via NBC News)

Science and technology

  • Exploration of Mercury
    • The European Space Agency announces that the BepiColombo spacecraft inserted itself into orbit around Mercury. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - November 14, 2026
item.description:
November 14, 2026 (2026-11-14) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Darfur campaign
      • Ahmed Abdallah Bishr, the general chief of staff for the Gathering of Sudan Liberation Forces (GSLF), dies of the wounds he suffered a month ago during an assassination attack by drone strike against his home in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan. (Sudan Tribune)
  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
      • The Iranian military attacks, with drones and missiles, an American military facility in Bahrain, in one of the largest attacks on the country in months. (The National News)

Arts and culture

  • Eurovision Song Contest Asia
    • The Philippines, with the song "Sobra-Sobra" by Carmelle, wins the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia held in Bangkok, Thailand. (AFP) (AP)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association threatens to indefinitely close unrest-affected factories without pay under the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006, after ongoing wage protests force the shutdown of 55 units and halt production at 147 others. (AFP via The Straits Times) (The Business Standard)
  • Canada–Philippines relations, Free trade agreements of Canada
    • Canadian prime minister Mark Carney announces that negotiations for a free-trade agreement (FTA) with the Philippines have concluded, with signing expected in 2027. The FTA would eliminate more than 90% of tariff lines. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • A bus overturns on the Garzón–Neiva highway in Colombia, killing six people and wounding eleven more. (AP)
  • Four workers are killed after a methane gas explosion at a mine in Chita, Boyacá Department, Colombia. (AP)
  • The Slagdijkstermolen windmill in Friesland, Netherlands, burns down. (Omrop Fryslân in Dutch)

Health and environment

  • Eight more people in Bangladesh are reported to have died from dengue fever, bringing this year's outbreak's death toll to 491. (BSS)

Law and crime

  • Crime in Bangladesh
    • Border Guard Bangladesh seize 48 high-power explosive gel sticks, 100 detonators, and 11 fuses during an operation along the Bangladesh–India border in Kanaighat Upazila, Sylhet District, Bangladesh. (BSS)
  • Crime in Guatemala
    • The Guatemalan Army begins deploying a battalion to the departments of Zacapa, Izabal, and Chiquimula following an attack in the Zacapa Department the previous day that killed five people. (Prensa Libre in Spanish)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French civil unrest
      • Student protesters, unions, and the yellow vests hold another nationwide protest in France, with over 100,000 participants. (France 24) (Türkiye)
  • 2027 South Sudanese general election
    • The South Sudanese election commission postpones the country's first presidential and parliamentary elections since independence in 2011 from December 22, 2026, to February 11, 2027, amid political tensions and continuing violence. (AFP via RFI)

Science and technology

  • The Italian Data Protection Authority fines American technology company Meta for €805 million (US$887 million) after it was found that the Facebook Android app had access to users' photos and videos without specific consent or disclosure. (BBC News) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - November 23, 2026
item.description:
November 23, 2026 (2026-11-23) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukraine launches a large-scale drone attack across western Russia, striking the Perm refinery in Perm Krai and Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov Oblast. (The Kyiv Independent) (The Moscow Times)
  • Colombian conflict
    • At least 21 people are injured after a car bomb explodes next to the Meta Department Government building in downtown Villavicencio, Colombia. (Anadolu Ajansi)
    • Three civilians are injured and 60 homes are damaged following a drone attack against a police station in Cúcuta. This is the first registered drone attack in an urban area in Colombia. (Colombia Reports)
  • Aftermath of the Bangladesh July Uprising
    • At least 30 people are injured, eight seriously, and 12 shops are vandalised as rival factions of the banned Awami League clash in two separate incidents and detonate four crude bombs in Gopalganj District, Bangladesh. (The Daily Star) (The Business Standard)
    • At least 15 people are injured and 28 houses and shops are vandalised during clashes between rival Bangladesh Nationalist Party factions in Shailkupa Upazila, Jhenaidah District, Bangladesh. (The Daily Star)
  • Kurdish–Turkish conflict
    • Turkish intelligence reports that the Kurdistan Workers' Party withdraws from 14 additional bases in northern Iraq as part of an ongoing disarmament process aimed at ending its conflict with Turkey. (AFP via France 24)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Mexican authorities announce that they have killed 16 suspected members of the Beltrán-Leyva cartel during an operation to capture former high-ranking leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, who was on the FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, in Guasave, Sinaloa, Mexico. (Voice of Emirates)
  • Sudanese nomadic conflicts
    • Five people are killed and six others are injured in a farmer–herder conflict in East Darfur, Sudan. (Radio Tamazuj)


Business and economy

  • Jensen Huang scandal, Chinese intelligence activity abroad
    • Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer less than two weeks after he resigned following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, who is suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China. (CBS)

Disasters and accidents

  • Seven people are killed and two others are injured after a truck loaded with stones overturns onto a minitruck in Bahawalpur District, Punjab, Pakistan. (Xinhua)
  • Five people are killed and 25 others are injured when a bus crashes on the Pan-American Highway outside of Ciudad Juárez, Mexico. (KTSM)

International relations

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Italian unrest
      • A 58-year-old student dies at Sapienza University in Rome, Italy, while being on a hunger strike protesting the fact that he had not been assigned a place to stay. (Fanpage in Italian)
  • Myanmar–United Kingdom relations, Rohingya genocide case
    • British foreign secretary Ed Miliband announces sanctions against five military leaders of Myanmar, while also granting recognition of the Rohingya genocide. (BBC News) (Daily Sun)
  • Tajikistan formally begins the process of withdrawing from the International Criminal Court. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis
    • The Supreme Court of Spain grants amnesty to former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, who is currently in self-imposed exile in Belgium, thereby bringing the legal proceedings against the leaders of the October 2017 declaration of independence to a definitive close. (CNN)
  • 2026 European bomb threat wave
    • Hundreds of schools across Denmark and Germany receive bomb threats via email, with police ordering the schools to continue operations as normal. (Reuters)
  • Women's rights in Iran
    • Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi receives 74 lashes for performing at a music concert without wearing a hijab. (BBC News)
  • The Superior Court of Quebec suspends a 2022 law making allegiance to Canada's monarch optional for provincial legislators, requiring them to swear an oath to King Charles III before sitting in the National Assembly. (AFP via France 24)
  • Eight people are injured in a tear gas attack at a meeting of the Alliance 90/The Greens political party in Schwerte, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. (Tagesschau)

Sports

  • 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids
    • In association football, FIFA confirms Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the United States as joint hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales will jointly host the 2035 tournament. (AFP)

item.title: Current Events - November 16, 2026
item.description:
November 16, 2026 (2026-11-16) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Saudi Arabia's King Salman appoints Chairman of the General Staff Fayyadh Al Ruwaili as commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, following the retreat of Yemeni government forces from areas near the Bab al-Mandeb to Aden. (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • 2026 Komyshuvakha strike
        • Ukraine finishes search and rescue operations at a humanitarian aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, that was destroyed by a Russian airstrike on 2 November. A total of 72 people were killed, and four more people are missing. (Meduza in Russian)
    • Crimea attacks
      • The Crimean Bridge is struck by a Ukrainian kamikaze drone, damaging the structure and prompting Russian authorities to close the bridge to vehicle traffic. The bridge is partially reopened later in the day. (BBC News) (The Guardian)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Five gunmen are killed after a shootout between criminal organizations in Chignahuapan, Puebla, Mexico. (El Sol de México in Spanish)
    • Two people are killed and three more injured in a mass shooting at a party in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico. (El Universal in Spanish)
  • Around ten people are injured, several requiring hospitalization, in East London, United Kingdom, when banned Awami League activists allegedly attack Bangladeshi expatriates and students with glass bottles and steel rods outside a reception for National Citizen Party convener Nahid Islam and the 11 Party Alliance. (New Age)

Arts and culture

  • English actor Robert Pattinson is cast as James Bond in the ongoing film series starring the character. (Variety)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • Police fire tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesting garment workers blocking a road in Gazipur, after the Minimum Wage Board postpones its scheduled minimum wage meeting. (The Daily Star) (The Business Standard)
  • The European Commission (EC) and the United States Federal Reserve approve Italian bank UniCredit's proposed €45 billion (US$49 billion) acquisition of Germany's Commerzbank, following the European Central Bank's approval in October. The EC grants unconditional antitrust clearance. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Patong fire
    • Eleven people are killed and 16 others are injured in a fire at a four-story building in Patong, Phuket province, Thailand. (Al Jazeera)
  • Three people are killed when a Piper Comanche aircraft crashes in the North Rim area of Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona, United States. (FOX Weather)

International relations

  • Somalia–United States relations, USAID in the second Trump administration, United States intervention in Somalia
    • The United States Department of State reverses its decision to withdraw funding from the United Nations Support Office for Somalia and supports extending its mandate and that of the African Union's military mission combating Al-Shabaab for another year. (AFP)
  • Former Togolese prime minister Gilbert Houngbo is re-elected director-general of the International Labour Organization. (AFP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
    • A Paraguayan judge orders impeached former president Santiago Peña transferred to the Viñas Cué military prison pending trial on charges of criminal association, breach of trust, and misuse of public office linked to Ueno Bank's collapse. (Reuters)
  • Crime in South Africa
    • Nine people are killed in a mass shooting at a shack near Pretoria, South Africa. (NBC News)
    • Eight people are found shot and killed inside a vehicle in Msunduzi Local Municipality, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. (AP)
  • Insurgency in Bahrain
    • Bahrain sentences 64 Shia Muslims, mostly clerics, to life in prison for establishing a terrorist group linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. (BBC News)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Gambian presidential election
    • The Gambian election commission approves President Adama Barrow's candidacy for a third term in the December 5 presidential election as the country's constitution does not limit presidential terms. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - November 20, 2026
item.description:
November 20, 2026 (2026-11-20) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations report that an oil tanker has been damaged and caught fire off Khasab, Oman, while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. (Al Jazeera)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • The Saudi-led coalition launches airstrikes on Hodeidah, Yemen, targeting weapons smuggling used by the Houthis, and on targets in the Sanaa, Saada, and Taiz governorates. (AP) (Al Jazeera)
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Yemeni government forces say they have conducted operations in the Al-Jawf, Marib, and Taiz governorates that have killed or injured 193 Houthi fighters. (Arab News)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile strikes a field near the village of Nowy Lipowiec in Lublin Voivodeship, Poland, around 60 miles from a Coalition of the Willing training excercise. Air raid alerts are issued in Lublin and Podkarpackie Voivodeship. (AOL)
  • Haitian conflict
    • Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
      • Three Salvadoran soldiers are killed and another is injured when explosives they are handling detonate. (La Prensa Gráfica)
      • The governments of Haiti and El Salvador agree to build three new prisons to incarcerate Haitian gang members. (AP)
  • Aftermath of the July Uprising
    • In Bangladesh, attackers vandalize, loot, and burn over fifty houses and several businesses belonging to banned Awami League members in Kalia Upazila, Narail District, including the residence of former MP Kabirul Haque Mukti, following the killings of two Bangladesh Nationalist Party leaders. (New Age)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Bayelsa boat disaster
    • Twenty-four people are killed and 24 more are rescued after a ship carrying funeral goers capsizes in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. (Arab News)

Law and crime

  • Mexican drug war
    • Mexican special forces arrest Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, leader of the drug cartel Los Mazatlecos and one of the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation's ten most-wanted fugitives, and two associates during an operation in Guasave, Sinaloa, triggering armed clashes with suspected cartel members. (AFP via France 24)
  • Former ship captain Francesco Schettino of the former Costa Concordia cruise ship is released from prison after nine years. (Euronews)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Italian unrest
      • A general strike is held in Italy, with protests in multiple cities across the country. (Rai News in Italian)
  • Politics of Iraq
    • Iraqi prime minister Ali al-Zaidi announces that an agreement has been reached with Kata'ib Hezbollah to establish a joint operations center and jointly station troops in Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, after having threatened to send Iraqi security forces into the group's stronghold. (Al Jazeera) (Al Jazeera)

Science and technology

  • Anthropic employee and mathematician Levent Alpöge releases a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The proof was created with assistance from Claude. (BBC News)

item.title: Current Events - November 13, 2026
item.description:
November 13, 2026 (2026-11-13) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
        • Iran says it has destroyed an early-warning radar in Bahrain as a retaliation for a United States strike on telecommunication infrastructure on Sirik. (Türkiye)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 New Orleans ship collision
    • A tanker and the cruise ship American Heritage collide in the Mississippi River of the United States. The cruise ship, carrying 130 people, sinks. All aboard the American Heritage survive, with some taken to local hospitals for treatment of minor injuries. (BBC News) (CNN)
  • 2026 FAA nationwide ground stop
    • The United States Federal Aviation Administration issues a nationwide ground stop for all flights due to "extraordinary circumstances involving communications failures". It is later lifted. (Bloomberg) (Reuters)
  • Twenty-six people are killed and eleven more are injured in a bus–truck collision in Golaghat, India. (Al Jazeera) (Xinhua)
  • Six people are killed and five more injured after an under-construction building partially collapses in Nairobi, Kenya. (Xinhua)

International relations

  • Guatemala–United States relations, Mexican drug war
    • The United States Department of State designates three Guatemalan criminal groups as foreign terrorist organizations for providing material support to Mexican cartels. (AFP via Macau Business)
  • Qatar–Turkey relations
    • Qatar and Turkey sign a defense pact in Istanbul. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Corruption in Hungary
    • Hungary's National Asset Recovery and Protection Office recovers cash worth around US$19.5 million, including 5 billion Ft, from various locations around the country as part of a bribery investigation into Miklós Seszták, who served as Minister of National Development under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán from 2014 to 2018. (Euronews) (Reuters)
  • In the United Kingdom, Metropolitan Police announce a criminal investigation into actor David Walliams about "alleged serious sexual offences". The police say they are separate to those investigated by ITN and The Guardian. (AP) (BBC News)

Sports

  • 2026–27 Segunda División
    • In association football, the Royal Spanish Football Federation suspends FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono for 12 matches following a collision with CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel during a November 2 match, which resulted in de Miguel's death. (Al Jazeera)
